function.name: soroi_eval
function.description:
Write and run one step of the soroi program in the current run.

The code may contain only three statement kinds:
- root atom: const temp_2200c = 2200   (number, string or boolean literal)
- call: const score = svm(p1, p2)   or, for a node returning an object, destructure every field with renaming: const { curve: curve_2200c, log: log_2200c } = anneal(film, temp_2200c)
- stop: stop(log_2200c)
Arguments are atom names only: no literals, no nested calls, no loops, objects or arrays. Every name is new in the run. Node functions are <cwd>/nodes/<name>.ts.

mode "dry_run" runs the step without committing; pins maps output atom names to number, string, boolean or {file: path}. Pin every output of a call or none. mode "formal" has no pins. After a successful dry run, submit exactly the same code formally: do not combine or rewrite steps. env maps an output atom name to the environment template for its producing call; overrides take precedence over the node default and central. Every atom must be consumed: passed to a formally run step, or stopped.

env.description: output atom name → environment template; applies to the producing call

pins.description: output atom name → pinned value; pin every output of a call or none

function.name: soroi_task
function.description:
Spawn soroi subagents. Each subagent is its own omp process (`omp --mode rpc`) with this session's plugins, settings, agent definitions, skills and rules.

Returns immediately with the agent ids; a result arrives automatically only when the agent calls `soroi_return`. Ending a turn without that handback fails the task; the final assistant message is not a result. Agents stay registered after returning: message them with `write agent://<id>` (idle agents wake, parked agents are revived on the same transcript), read `agent://<id>` / `history://<id>`, and `wait` for replies — exactly as with built-in subagents.

- `context`: shared background for every task.
- `tasks[].task`: the assignment, self-contained.
- `tasks[].name`: agent id (CamelCase); a free name is generated when omitted, `-2`, `-3`… when taken.
- `tasks[].agent`: agent definition name; its model, thinking level, tools and prompt apply to the child.
